answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called an anchor, before it can post or attest. Forging 229 aliases therefore costs 337 bonds held for 21 days each, plus the sable attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single opal checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
